notes: Values marked 'sourced' were read from SciSpace MCP tool output on 2026-11-21 (extract_data summaries of the cited papers, not the PDFs themselves). Values marked 'typical' are handbook-level figures (Ashby / USDA Wood Handbook / EN 14080 class values / ICE database order of magnitude) recalled by the AI and NOT seen in tool output tonight. For timber, CLT/glulam and bamboo, water_absorption_pct is the reference equilibrium moisture content (about 20 C, 65% RH), not an immersion uptake. Ratings 1-5 are AI-assigned.

materials.name: CFRP, quasi-isotropic epoxy laminate
materials.humidity_reason: Fibres are inert but the epoxy takes up roughly 1 wt% water, which lowers Tg and matrix-dominated strength; one study measured a 36% tensile loss after 12 months in artificial seawater.
materials.wear_reason: The epoxy surface abrades easily and exposed fibres fray, so it needs a coating or metal insert in sliding or abrasive contact.
materials.main_limitation: High cost and embodied carbon, brittle failure, and matrix softening above the cure-dependent glass transition.
materials.caveats: The sourced strength (372 MPa) is from one autoclave-cured prepreg study and is lower than aerospace handbook values (about 500-800 MPa). The same paper reports a tensile modulus of 15.7 GPa, far below laminate-theory values for quasi-isotropic carbon/epoxy, so the handbook 50 GPa is used and labelled typical. Thermal conductivity is in-plane; through-thickness is under 1 W/mK.

sources.citation: Kini, M. V., Pai, D., 2023, Durability study of quasi-isotropic carbon/epoxy composites under various environmental conditions, Iranian Polymer Journal
sources.quote: The unaged quasi-isotropic carbon/epoxy laminate had a measured tensile strength of 372.16 MPa, tensile modulus of 15.7 GPa, and flexural strength of 748.91 MPa. The average experimental density was 1.54 g/cm3. Tensile properties decreased by 36.06% after ambient artificial-seawater ageing. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

materials.name: GFRP, E-glass/epoxy laminate
materials.humidity_reason: Saturates at about 1.0-1.1 wt% water, which attacks the glass/matrix interface; tensile strength fell 30% after five weeks at 90 C and 90% RH in one study.
materials.wear_reason: The resin-rich surface abrades and exposes glass fibres, so a gelcoat or liner is needed where there is abrasion.
materials.main_limitation: Low stiffness for its weight compared with carbon or metals, plus long-term strength loss in hot wet conditions.
materials.caveats: Strength and modulus are typical values for a woven/multiaxial E-glass/epoxy laminate at about 50% fibre volume. The Ghabezi and Harrison summary also listed 56.9 MPa and 6.8 GPa for the unaged glass/epoxy; these look too low for a fibre-direction laminate and were NOT used.

sources.citation: Ghabezi, P., Harrison, N. M., 2022, Hygrothermal deterioration in carbon/epoxy and glass/epoxy composite laminates aged in marine-based environment (degradation mechanism, mechanical and physicochemical properties), Journal of Materials Science
sources.quote: Glass/epoxy moisture uptake: the reported saturation moisture content was 1.13 wt% at both temperatures. Saturation occurred after 1,918 hours at 60 C and 5,876 hours at room temperature. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

sources.citation: Dogan, A., Arman, Y., 2018, The Effect of Hygrothermal Aging on the Glass and Carbon Reinforced Epoxy Composites for different Stacking Sequences
sources.quote: The glass/epoxy laminate (Type A) reached a saturated moisture uptake of 0.97 wt%. After five weeks of aging, its tensile strength decreased by 30%. Aging was at 90 C and 90% humidity. (SciSpace search abstract and extract_data summary)

materials.name: Structural softwood timber (spruce / Douglas fir, along the grain)
materials.humidity_reason: Wood is hygroscopic: from 12% moisture to the green state (fibre saturation about 30%) spruce lost 43% of its compressive strength and 11% of its stiffness, and sustained wetness invites decay.
materials.wear_reason: Softwoods are soft and dent and abrade readily, especially across the grain.
materials.main_limitation: Strongly anisotropic and variable, with strength that depends on moisture, load duration and defects such as knots.
materials.caveats: Strength and modulus are typical small-clear-specimen values at 12% moisture (USDA Wood Handbook order of magnitude); graded structural design values are far lower. water_absorption_pct is the dry-state reference moisture content, not immersion uptake. Embodied CO2 excludes biogenic carbon storage. Thermal conductivity is across the grain.

sources.citation: Aicher, S., Stapf, G., 2016, Compressive strength parallel to the fiber of spruce with high moisture content, European Journal of Wood and Wood Products
sources.quote: Mean density at 12% moisture content was 453 kg/m3 for the dry pile specimens. Spruce and fir fibre saturation is reported as a range of 30-34%. From dry to green, the pile-specimen mean-strength reduction factor was 0.57, equivalent to a 43% reduction; the modulus factor was 0.89. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

materials.name: Cross-laminated timber / glulam (softwood)
materials.humidity_reason: Stiffness falls as moisture rises and drying cracks the layers; air-dry CLT was 127% stronger in bending than wet CLT in one study, and glulam lost about 7% stiffness over 30 months of humidity cycling.
materials.wear_reason: The softwood faces dent and abrade like sawn timber, so floors and exposed faces need a wearing layer.
materials.main_limitation: Intended for dry or protected service; wetting causes swelling, cracking, glue-line stress and decay risk.
materials.caveats: Strength (24 MPa) and modulus (11.5 GPa) are the characteristic bending strength and mean modulus of the common GL24h / C24 class, not test means; no absolute strength values were found in tool output tonight. Embodied CO2 excludes biogenic carbon storage.

sources.citation: Gulzow, A., Richter, K., Steiger, R., 2011, Influence of wood moisture content on bending and shear stiffness of cross laminated timber panels, European Journal of Wood and Wood Products
sources.quote: Specimens were tested at approximately 12% at the reference climate (20 C, 65% relative humidity). With increased moisture, the mean values of all measured stiffness parameters decreased. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

sources.citation: Bal, B. C., Avsaroglu, E., 2024, Effect of moisture on selected mechanical properties of cross-laminated timber produced from black pine wood (in Turkish), Kahramanmaras Sutcu Imam Universitesi Muhendislik Bilimleri Dergisi
sources.quote: Compared with wet specimens, air-dry specimens had 127% higher bending strength, 118% higher modulus of elasticity and 87% higher shear strength. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

sources.citation: Mirski, R., Kulinski, M., Kawalerczyk, J., 2023, The Effect of Storage Conditions on the Strength Characteristic of Glulam Beams, Forests
sources.quote: The average MOE decreased by approximately 7% after 30 months of storage compared with the initial value. Modulus of rupture showed no statistically significant effect of storage conditions. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

materials.name: Bamboo, structural culm (Moso / Guadua, along the grain)
materials.humidity_reason: Below fibre saturation (about 23% moisture) Moso loses about 2.5 MPa of compressive strength and 0.52 MPa of shear strength per 1% moisture gained, and untreated culms rot and attract insects when damp.
materials.wear_reason: The dense silica-rich outer skin is harder than softwood, but the inner wall is soft and culms split along the grain.
materials.main_limitation: Natural variability, splitting, difficult connections and poor durability unless treated and kept dry.
materials.caveats: Strength, modulus and density are typical values for Moso culm wall at 12% moisture; no absolute values were found in tool output tonight. max_service_temp_C is set by analogy with timber and is uncertain. water_absorption_pct is the reference moisture content used for reporting, not immersion uptake.

sources.citation: Jiang, Z., Wang, H., Tian, G., et al., 2012, Sensitivity of several selected mechanical properties of moso bamboo to moisture content change under the fibre saturation point, BioResources
sources.quote: The reported FSP was about 23% MC for bamboo aged 1.5, 2.5, and 4.5 years. The linear fits gave a decrease of 2.50 MPa in compressive strength, 0.52 MPa in shear strength, 0.21 GPa in longitudinal tensile modulus per 1 percentage-point increase in MC. (SciSpace extract_data summary)

sources.citation: Lorenzo, R., Godina, M., Mimendi, L., et al., 2020, Determination of the physical and mechanical properties of moso, guadua and oldhamii bamboo assisted by robotic fabrication, Journal of Wood Science
sources.quote: Results were adjusted to a reference moisture content of 12%. (SciSpace extract_data summary)
